name: CAMBODIA

flag.title: Flag of Cambodia
flag.note: Red centre, blue edges; Angkor Wat in white

lead: Cambodia is in the heart of Southeast Asia. The Mekong River flows past jungles that hide Angkor Wat, one of the world's greatest wonders.
geo: Cambodia is mostly flat lowlands watered by the Mekong River. Tonle Sap is Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. It swells to six times its dry-season size in the monsoon (rainy season).
The Cardamom Mountains rise in the southwest and shelter dense rainforest. About 20% of the land is farmed, mostly rice paddies (flooded fields).
animals: The Irrawaddy dolphin is chubby and looks like it is smiling. It lives only in a short stretch of the Mekong near Kratie. About 100 survive, and Cambodians see them as sacred.
The giant ibis, Cambodia's national bird, is nearly as tall as a child. It is close to dying out and nests in northern forests.
culture: Cambodians greet each other with a sampeah. They press their palms together and bow a little.
Khmer food is built around prahok, a soured fish paste nicknamed 'Cambodian cheese'. Fish amok is the dish visitors remember most.
history: In 802 CE, King Jayavarman II declared himself god-king and began the Khmer Empire. Over 600 years, it grew to cover much of mainland Southeast Asia.
Thai invaders ended the empire in 1431. Cambodia later became a colony of France. In the 1970s, the Khmer Rouge, a cruel ruling group, caused terrible loss of life.
wows: The world's largest religious monument is Angkor Wat. It covers 162 hectares (1.6 km²), with a moat over 5 km.
Cambodia's flag shows a real building, the towers of Angkor Wat, as its main picture.
The Tonle Sap River reverses direction twice a year when Mekong floods push water upstream.
In the 13th century, Angkor was the biggest city before factories, as wide as modern Los Angeles.
Cambodia has no McDonald's, one of the last Southeast Asian countries without a branch.
Unlike Vietnamese and Thai, Khmer has no tones. A voice's pitch cannot change a word's meaning.
Cambodian weddings last three full days.

myths.myth: Angkor Wat was a lost city forgotten for centuries
myths.fact: People kept living and praying there. European explorers made it famous abroad in the 1800s.

myths.myth: Angkor Wat was always a Buddhist temple
myths.fact: King Suryavarman II built it for the Hindu god Vishnu in the early 1100s. It became Buddhist later.
